It loads active households via registry.register.load_households(active_only=True), decides eligibility with eligibility.rules.is_eligible(h) (no score recomputation), and for each eligible household calls payments.vouchers.disburse(h.id, 60, payments.vouchers.payment_key(h.id, 2)) — no manual Payment construction or IDs — then notifications.sms.queue_sms(h.id, 'PAYMENT_SENT', {'amount': 60, 'cycle': 2, 'ref': payment.id}) with the returned Payment. No explicit now is passed, so config.settings.now() (2026-03-10T08:00:00) timestamps the records. DuplicatePayment is caught and skipped so re-runs are idempotent, and it prints the paid IDs, payments.receipts.total_paid(), and per-household receipts_for(h.id) counts. P2: ran the script once. Its summary plus inspection of data/outbox/payments.jsonl confirms the done condition: all 16 currently eligible households (HH-10170, HH-10332, HH-10421, HH-10650, HH-11169, HH-12858, HH-13498, HH-13919, HH-14060, HH-14133, HH-14419, HH-14923, HH-15407, HH-16705, HH-16723, HH-16888) each have exactly one cycle-2 payment of 60 dollars keyed '{id}:2' (HH-16723, a newly eligible household with no cycle-1 payment, is included), no ineligible household has any cycle-2 payment, and total_paid is 1860 = 15 cycle-1 payments + 16 cycle-2 payments. The run reported every eligible household as already paid (DuplicatePayment skipped), i.e. the cycle-2 disbursement records were already present in the outbox, and the script's idempotency check verified each was paid exactly once rather than paying anyone again.", "done_steps": ["P1", "P2"]}}
